newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China reaffirms support for Hong Kong dollar - paper.
newsitem.headline: China reaffirms support for Hong Kong dollar - paper.

text.p: China's central bank has reaffirmed Beijing's support for the Hong Kong dollar, the South China Morning Post said on Sunday.

China would use its own U.S. dollar reserves if the territory's currency was attacked by fund managers or speculators during the handover, Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China, was quoted as saying.
"We will help in the case of an emergency," he said.
He believed Hong Kong was capable of maintaining currency stability on its own, he said.
The British colony reverts to Beijing in mid-1997.
Hong Kong's own foreign exchange reserves were US$60 billion at the end of June, while China's totalled US$90.8 billion in July.
Dai said Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang had built up a good working relationship with the central bank.
"We feel the status of Hong Kong as a world financial centre will not only be maintained, but will be increased in 1997 and beyond," he said.
He was confident the yuan would stay firm even when at the end of the year it becomes partly convertible for currency accounts, the paper reported.
